description: REQ-204's Tier-0 acceptance criterion (behavioral-spec.md lines 508-515) claims self-sufficiency it does not actually have: 'Because a "section" is defined as a heading line through, but not including, the next "## " heading line, the absence of BOTH heading substrings is definitionally equivalent to the absence of the two sections' entire bodies -- there is no separate "and also check the body" step, and therefore no residual-phrase judgment call for either of these two sections.' This is only true if the section was deleted as one atomic heading+body edit. As a pure structural check, 'no line is a heading containing substring X' does NOT, by itself, prove the corresponding BODY paragraphs are also gone -- deleting only the heading line (leaving the body lines 90-96/99-103 in place) would cause those body lines to silently become a headerless continuation of whichever section precedes them (e.g. merged into the retained '## Your earn tools' section, or floating with no heading at all), which would still make PROP-204a's Tier-0 check (heading-substring-absence) PASS while every imperative sentence in that body ('your FIRST action this wake MUST be economy/gig...', 'Do this BEFORE hl_trade / yield / anything else', 'Re-yielding every wake = failure.') remains verbatim in buildSystemPrompt's actual output. REQ-204's text presents this as a property of PROP-204a alone ('there is no separate... step'), when in fact the only thing that would catch this specific naive-deletion failure mode is PROP-203b's SEPARATE full-file generic-marker re-scan (a different proof obligation, in a different table row) -- a real dependency REQ-204's own acceptance criteria never states as a DEPENDS-ON relationship. If a Phase 3 reviewer (or an automated check) treats PROP-204a's Tier-0 result as self-contained and sufficient, exactly as REQ-204's own wording invites, an incomplete deletion (heading removed, body orphaned) would be scored as satisfying REQ-204 while the actual steering content the requirement exists to remove is still present verbatim in the shipped prompt.

evidence.snippet: 'Because a "section" is defined as a heading line through, but not including, the next "## " heading line, the absence of BOTH heading substrings is definitionally equivalent to the absence of the two sections' entire bodies -- there is no separate "and also check the body" step, and therefore no residual-phrase judgment call for either of these two sections.'
